definitions.explanation: A division of the academic year.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{学期|がっき}が{始|はじ}まりました。
1{学期|がっき}の{成績|せいせき}は{良|よ}かったです。
examples.english: My grades for the first term were good.

examples.japanese: {学期|がっき}の{終|お}わりに{試験|しけん}があります。
examples.english: There are exams at the end of the term.

examples.japanese: 2{学期|がっき}から{部活|ぶかつ}を{始|はじ}めようと{思|おも}っています。
examples.english: I'm thinking of starting a club activity from the second term.

examples.japanese: {学期|がっき}が{変|か}わるたびに、{先生|せんせい}から{新|あたら}しい{教科書|きょうかしょ}をもらいます。
examples.english: Every time the term changes, we receive new textbooks from the teacher.

notes:
{学期|がっき} means semester or school term.

WORD FORMATION:
{学|がく} (study) + {期|き} (period).

JAPANESE SCHOOL SYSTEM:
Most Japanese schools use a three-term system:
- 1{学期|がっき} ({一学期|いちがっき}): April–July
- 2{学期|がっき} ({二学期|にがっき}): September–December
- 3{学期|がっき} ({三学期|さんがっき}): January–March

Some universities use a two-semester system:
- {前期|ぜんき}: first semester (spring)
- {後期|こうき}: second semester (fall)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {学期|がっき}の{始|はじ}まり: start of the term
- {学期|がっき}の{終|お}わり: end of the term
- {学期末|がっきまつ}: end of term
- {学期末|がっきまつ}{試験|しけん}: end-of-term exams

CULTURAL NOTE: The Japanese school year starts in April, coinciding with the cherry blossom season.
